focus_details.name: Macerich

key_dates.note: Watch: SNO pipeline conversion, Forever 21 re-leasing progress
Term loan refinancing — watch spread vs SOFR

thesis_points: Quality over speed: replacing Forever 21 vacancies (~570K sqft) with experiential anchors at >2x legacy rents
New CEO Jackson Hsieh (ex-Spirit Realty) reduced ND/EBITDA from 10.8x → 7.8x within ~1 year of taking office
Crabtree acquisition: fortress-quality asset at $219/SF vs $261/SF peer, 11% going-in cap rate vs ~7-8% peers
Portfolio moat: 42 Class A malls in prime coastal metros (CA, NY, AZ, NJ, PA), $894/SF go-forward tenant sales
16 consecutive quarters of positive leasing spreads; SNO pipeline $90–140M+; new leases 9% above renewals
Deleveraging roadmap: $6.6B → ~$4.5B debt by 2029–2030, targeting ~6x ND/EBITDA via asset sales

key_debate.street: High leverage (8.2x vs SPG 5.7x, SKT 5.4x), tenant bankruptcies (Forever 21, Claire's) signal structural decline
key_debate.our_view: Occupancy gap is deliberate — quality tenants commanding >2x prior rents. Deleveraging credibly underway with $395M B/C sales in 2025

overview.narrative:
REITs traded mixed Tuesday with a clear defensive tilt toward housing and towers while office and retail lagged. Housing led all subsectors at +1.22% on average, powered by LEN's +3.07% move likely tied to favorable new home sales data, while towers gained +0.76% with AMT surging +2.85% as the long-duration trade caught a bid on softening rate expectations. Industrial and retail both slipped modestly, each down roughly 15-20bps.

The standout divergences demand attention. FSP's +9.80% spike in an otherwise negative office tape (avg -0.16%) screams idiosyncratic catalyst — likely a disposition announcement or activist development — while HPP cratered -3.55% at the other extreme. Healthcare saw a remarkable 700bp spread between ARE (+5.08%) and VTR (-1.97%), suggesting rotation from senior housing into life science assets. UNIT's -3.34% decline continued to weigh on an otherwise constructive tower session, reinforcing the fiber vs. macro tower bifurcation.

For Wednesday positioning, the housing and tower leadership suggests the market is pricing in a more dovish Fed trajectory, favoring duration-sensitive names. We'd lean into AMT strength and housing momentum while staying cautious on office ex-FSP. Watch for mean reversion in VTR after today's outsized underperformance, and monitor FSP for follow-through to determine whether today's move has legs or fades.
